questions.prompt: When Boston requires usable outdoor space for each family dwelling, what parts of the lot can be counted toward it?
choices: Front, side, and rear yards not used for an accessory building, parking, or driveway
The entire lot including parking spaces
Public sidewalks next to the property
questions.answer: Front, side, and rear yards not used for an accessory building, parking, or driveway
questions.excerpt:
Where a minimum usable open space per dwelling unit is specified in this code, there
               shall be allotted and maintained for lawful outdoor uses other than off-street parking
               on every lot within the district, and devoted to the use, specified, for each dwelling
               unit intended for family occupancy the minimum usable open space so specified, except
               that in H-2-65, H-3-65, H-3, H-4 and H-5 districts all or part of this requirement
               may be met by suitably designed and accessible space on balconies of main buildings
               or on the roofs of wings of main buildings or on the roofs of accessory buildings.

               not devoted to an accessory building or off-street parking or driveway purposes shall
               be included in computing usable open space for the purposes of this article. (As amended on February 17, 1971, July 9, 1973, October 31, 1980, and April 27, 1990)

               requirements of this code with respect to Usable Open Space shall apply as if each
               Dwelling or Main Building were on a separate Lot. (As inserted on December 22, 2003)
